newsitem.title: USA: Nord Pacific production up, costs down.
newsitem.headline: Nord Pacific production up, costs down.

text.p: Nord Pacific Ltd said Wednesday copper production at its 40 percent owned Girilambone copper mine, New South Wales, Australia, reached a record 10.3 million pounds during the fourth quarter of 1996.
That is up 54 percent from the fourth quarter of 1995, the company pointed out. Average cash cost of production was $0.37 per pound, 31 percent lower than in the previous quarter.
Production for the full year 1996 was 35.9 million pounds, up 27 percent from full year 1995, Nord Pacific said.
"The result was the best on record for the mine, President Pierce Carson said.
"We attribute the production increase and lower costs to innovative leaching techniques recently implemented and believe production will continue at these higher levels for the foreseeable future."
Nord Pacific said there has been continuing exploration success at the 50 percent owned Tritton project 12 miles southwest of the Girilambone mine.
The resource has been estimated at 9.75 million tonnes grading 3.01 percent copper, 0.21 grams/tonne gold and 11 grams/tonne silver, the company said.

Exploration and development drilling has confirmed copper mineralization to a depth of 1,000 meters, with mineralization still open below that level, it continued, noting the resource now stands at 646 million pounds of contained copper.
Nord Pacific said construction of the Simberi gold mine planned to commence in 1997 with initial production of gold anticipated in early 1998.

At the Ramu Nickel-Cobalt Project, in which Nord Pacific has 35 percent equity, emphasis was directed at securing a major equity co-venturer with the ability to contribute financial strength and expertise through a bankable feasibility study and ultimate development.
